meta.source: AI Freedom Summit 2026 (AIFS Kelowna) talk transcripts, Jeff's slide photos, and the AIFS resources page agent prompts
meta.note: Checklist items and quotes come from the talks. Owners are role placeholders. Status reflects what exists today; update it in the dashboard (saved on this device) and export.

categories.a: Systems, agents and prompts to build
categories.b: Dashboard views, fields, scorecards and metrics

items.item: Run the Money Prompt: connect AI to the inbox and systems and ask it to find money leaks (double charges, unused subscriptions)
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: Find ways to save me money. Scan my email, scan my systems, and identify ways to save me money.
items.prompt: Find ways to save me money. Scan my email, scan my systems, and identify ways to save me money.

items.item: Install the Constraint Finder / business constraint agent that names the ONE constraint, posts it in Slack, tags the team and learns from their replies
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: It identifies it every Sunday night and Thursday, because Thursday I want to see if they solved it, posted it in Slack for the teams, tags everybody.

items.item: Work every problem through the Money Constraint Loop: Locate, Diagnose, Quantify, Prescribe, Execute
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: So first off, we have to locate it. Then we need to diagnose.
items.note: Constraint view added to dashboard (example data).

items.item: Give every agent a learning loop: it posts its output, the team replies with feedback, the feedback goes back into the agent
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: If you don't have a learning loop, you don't have an agent. You have an automation.

items.item: Ask for feedback in every agent message: "Reply to this message with your feedback"
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: Reply to this message with your feedback

items.item: Build data equity: for every workflow, save an example of the input and a great output (from your best people, not the average)
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: every workflow has to have a data example of what an input and great output looks like

items.item: Split bots by role (one job each) and separate personal bots from team bots
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: In the same way you have people on your team, you should have personal bots, that's what these are, and you should have team bots.

items.item: Bot that reviews all bots every week and says which to merge
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: I have a bot that analyzes my bots every week and tells me which ones I should merge into other bots

items.item: Skills bot that spots skills the bots should share
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: I have a skills bot that looks at all the things my bots are doing and identify skills it should create

items.item: First bot to build = the next person you'd hire; program it like a hire with your SOPs
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: I always ask them, "Who's the person you need to hire next?"

items.item: Inbox manager bot with written limits on what it may share
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: I have an inbox manager bot that my chief of staff has access to, that has access to everything, but I gave it some constraints

items.item: Team Trainer bot: finds what the team struggles with, ranks topics by money and people affected, outlines the training
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 2, Become an AI Leader
items.quote: finds the things that would make me the most money, that would affect the most people, prioritizes them
items.prompt: (Workbook prompt) identify within your company what you need to teach and then give you the outline so you can teach it

items.item: Client Host agent: reads every customer system each morning and lists who needs a touch today, with drafts waiting for approval
items.speaker: Simon Ogilvie
items.talk: Simon Ogilvie, Day 2, Raving Fans Blueprint
items.quote: Client Host analyzes your entire client database every day
items.prompt: (Jeff's slide photo) Connect data, explain what's where, define purple/green/yellow/red, schedule 8 AM top 9 = 3 green / 3 yellow / 3 red. Use only what's in the data. Never invent customers or quotes. Never send anything. I approve every message.
items.note: Dashboard Client Host view built with example data; agent not connected yet.

items.item: Client Host setup step 1-2: connect your data and tell the agent what lives where
items.speaker: Simon Ogilvie
items.talk: Simon Ogilvie, Day 2, Raving Fans Blueprint
items.quote: connect your data, wherever it is, whatever you've got. Explain to the agent what's where in the business.

items.item: Client Host setup step 3-4: define what green and yellow look like, then pick the schedule and format
items.speaker: Simon Ogilvie
items.talk: Simon Ogilvie, Day 2, Raving Fans Blueprint
items.quote: What does green look like? What does yellow look like? What typically causes people to get stuck? And then just pick your schedule.

items.item: Silent churn search: find customers not heard from in 30/90 days; look for no replies, no rebooks, no reviews
items.speaker: Simon Ogilvie
items.talk: Simon Ogilvie, Day 2, Raving Fans Blueprint
items.quote: go and find the people that we haven't heard from in the last 30 days, in the last 90 days
items.prompt: Go and find the people that we haven't heard from in the last 30 days, in the last 90 days. Who hasn't sent an email? Who hasn't answered an email? Who hasn't answered their support tickets? Look for no replies, no rebooks, no reviews.

items.item: Drafts wait for a human to edit and send; assign each next step to a team member
items.speaker: Simon Ogilvie
items.talk: Simon Ogilvie, Day 2, Raving Fans Blueprint
items.quote: you can have those emails drafted, waiting for you to edit and put that taste, that care back into it

items.item: AI brain step 1, capture: record meeting transcripts and notes
items.speaker: Graeme Barlow
items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula
items.quote: Whatever you end up using, step one is capture.
items.note: Granola notes exist; brain not built.

items.item: AI brain step 2, organize: a nightly loop that sorts, rebuilds and links the brain
items.speaker: Graeme Barlow
items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula
items.quote: We want to have a loop that runs every night that sorts, rebuilds, and organizes your brain.

items.item: AI brain step 3, connect it to company playbooks (Notion / Google Drive / wiki)
items.speaker: Graeme Barlow
items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula
items.quote: The third is connect.

items.item: AI brain step 4, refresh: have the AI interview you daily about gaps and confusion
items.speaker: Graeme Barlow
items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula
items.quote: have your AI, whichever one you've decided to use to manage ingestion and capture in your brain, interview you daily
items.prompt: Have the AI ask you: What are the gaps? What don't you understand? What's missing? What's confusing?

items.item: Chief of Staff agent that orchestrates and follows up but does not do the work itself
items.speaker: Graeme Barlow
items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula
items.quote: you do not want your chief of staff to be the agent that is doing the work
items.note: Grok Bot runs as chief of staff today.

items.item: Chief of Staff checks every other agent is alive and doing its job
items.speaker: Graeme Barlow
items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula
items.quote: Go poke all the other agents and make sure they're alive.

items.item: AI scout agent that watches for better AI tools and reports to the chief of staff (proposes only; no new installs without approval)
items.speaker: Graeme Barlow
items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula
items.quote: Its entire job is scan the entire internet, find everything new happening every day and every week in AI

items.item: Deal Coach: review the last 30 days of calls plus CRM activity and turn winners' behavior into a playbook
items.speaker: Aubtin Sharifpour
items.talk: Aubtin Sharifpour, Day 1, Revenue Engine Autopilot
items.quote: review the last 30 days of calls, compare CRM activity, and then turn your winning behaviors into a playbook

items.item: Deal Coach daily audit: are reps filling in call recordings, CRM and activity?
items.speaker: Aubtin Sharifpour
items.talk: Aubtin Sharifpour, Day 1, Revenue Engine Autopilot
items.quote: Can you do a daily audit to make sure that people are filling out their call recordings, the CRM, and their activity
items.prompt: Can you do a daily audit to make sure that people are filling out their call recordings, the CRM, and their activity inside of HubSpot?

items.item: Deal Coach weekly coaching message to each rep from their numbers
items.speaker: Aubtin Sharifpour
items.talk: Aubtin Sharifpour, Day 1, Revenue Engine Autopilot
items.quote: a weekly coaching message, where it goes through everyone's numbers

items.item: Pre-call quiz prompt: from your won calls, build a quiz that shows the prospect where their pain is
items.speaker: Aubtin Sharifpour
items.talk: Aubtin Sharifpour, Day 1, Revenue Engine Autopilot
items.quote: based on all my calls, what questions could I ask someone before their call and make it in a quiz format to help them understand where their pain is?
items.prompt: Based on all my calls, what questions could I ask someone before their call and make it in a quiz format to help them understand where their pain is?

items.item: Creative Strategist agent: mine real customer words into message ideas, scripts and ads
items.speaker: Matt Bertulli
items.talk: Matt Bertulli, Day 1, Scale the Unscalable
items.quote: So a creative strategist, this is an agent that you absolutely need to create.

items.item: One research agent per pain point / customer type, and a creative strategist per product
items.speaker: Matt Bertulli
items.talk: Matt Bertulli, Day 1, Scale the Unscalable
items.quote: I have one research agent per pain point in ICP

items.item: AI Content Strategist: match outlier content with customer calls, then write Hook-Explain-Illustrate-Teach scripts
items.speaker: Sam Gaudet
items.talk: Sam Gaudet, Day 2, The Authority Brand
items.quote: This is our exact content strategist agent.

items.item: Mine comments (Instagram, Facebook, etc.) with an agent for content ideas
items.speaker: Sam Gaudet
items.talk: Sam Gaudet, Day 2, The Authority Brand
items.quote: And if you're not mining your comments, and you can use an agent for this

items.item: Map prompt: have AI map the business/funnel as a picture in plain words
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 2, Q&A + Close
items.quote: My favorite prompt is to draw this to me as a picture and use words at seventh-grade English.
items.prompt: Draw this to me as a picture and use words at seventh-grade English. / Look at my social media, help me map the funnel, help me understand the economics, help me understand free cash flow. Give me a financial model that allows me to do a million a month.

items.item: Install the digital-download prompts: give your AI the links and say "Install this"
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 2, Q&A + Close
items.quote: you copy those two links and you give it to your AI and you say, "Install this,"
items.note: Resources page harvested into /workspace/aifs-resources/agents (7 agent prompts).

items.item: Build custom software only where it is unique to the business: a cockpit for agents; don't rebuild a CRM
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, Levels of AI
items.quote: that software becomes the cockpit for my agents to sit on top of

items.item: One single source of truth for the whole team (not fragmented)
items.speaker: Simon Ogilvie
items.talk: Simon Ogilvie, Day 2, Raving Fans Blueprint
items.quote: A single source of truth.
items.note: Also Jeff's 'One source of truth' slide photo. v1 built with example data.

items.item: Every initiative gets a dashboard; define the goal first
items.speaker: Graeme Barlow
items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula
items.quote: Every initiative in your organizations, big or small, needs a dashboard, and it needs clarity.

items.item: For each metric: define success, define the pace you must hit per day/hour, then ask AI to build the dashboard
items.speaker: Graeme Barlow
items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula
items.quote: how many feet every day or every hour do we need to move that would tell us we're on pace

items.item: Color everything: green = on pace, yellow = needs attention, red = the number one constraint
items.speaker: Graeme Barlow
items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula
items.quote: If it's red, we just found our number one constraint.

items.item: Every metric has an owner (name and phone) who knows how to move it
items.speaker: Graeme Barlow
items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula
items.quote: Every metric on your dashboard needs an owner. That means a name and a phone number.

items.item: Balance revenue with retention, satisfaction, quality and active usage
items.speaker: Graeme Barlow
items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula
items.quote: if you don't balance that measure with retention and customer satisfaction and quality

items.item: Unit-economics sensors on red/yellow/green: initial cash collected, accounts receivable, CAC, CAC payback
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, Levels of AI
items.quote: And my dashboard is red, green, yellow, and it'll turn yellow or red

items.item: Sales pipeline numbers: booked calls, qualified leads, show-ups, follow-ups per rep, close rate
items.speaker: Aubtin Sharifpour
items.talk: Aubtin Sharifpour, Day 1, Revenue Engine Autopilot
items.quote: Did we get enough book calls? Did we get enough qualified leads? Did they even show up to their calls?

items.item: Talent dashboard: applicants, open roles, volume and time at each stage
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, Levels of AI
items.quote: We have a dashboard, no different than the sales dashboard, for just talent

items.item: Constraint dashboard: show where the problem is (Locate) and run the loop as a team
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: We instrument the dashboard. What is the dashboard? The locate.

items.item: Quiet-customer cost: quiet customers x monthly value, doubled for lost referrals
items.speaker: Simon Ogilvie
items.talk: Simon Ogilvie, Day 2, Raving Fans Blueprint

items.item: Client traffic light, plus purple for raving fans (workbook/slide)
items.speaker: Simon Ogilvie
items.talk: Simon Ogilvie, Day 2, Raving Fans Blueprint
items.quote: Just go with a simple traffic light system.

items.item: Record 'what winning looks like' signals: thank-you emails, logins, renewals, asking for guidance
items.speaker: Simon Ogilvie
items.talk: Simon Ogilvie, Day 2, Raving Fans Blueprint
items.quote: Make a note that that's what winning looks like.

items.item: Show who is waiting on us (help desk, unanswered email, someone out sick)
items.speaker: Simon Ogilvie
items.talk: Simon Ogilvie, Day 2, Raving Fans Blueprint
items.quote: then we can't see who's waiting

items.item: Know the dollar cost of not solving the constraint
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: What is it costing me not to solve the problem?

items.item: Track what level of AI each person works at: chat, automate, agents, orchestrate, innovate
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, Levels of AI
items.quote: So what percent of your team currently is only using chat

items.item: Know the hours/cost of your current content process
items.speaker: Sam Gaudet
items.talk: Sam Gaudet, Day 2, The Authority Brand
items.quote: How many hours are you spending on a bad content process?

items.item: Draw the dashboard together with the team before building it
items.speaker: Aubtin Sharifpour
items.talk: Aubtin Sharifpour, Day 1, Revenue Engine Autopilot
items.quote: So we sat there and drew out the dashboard on this whiteboard

items.item: Install Grok Bot (or Claude / ChatGPT)
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model

items.item: Connect your agents to email and calendar
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model
items.quote: your agents connected to your email and your

items.talk: Aubtin Sharifpour, Day 1, Revenue Engine Autopilot
items.quote: Number two is a CRM. I use HubSpot, close.com.

items.item: Business brain in Notion; personal brain (Apex/Obsidian)
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model

items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, Levels of AI

items.talk: Simon Ogilvie, Day 2, Raving Fans Blueprint

items.item: AI video/motion tools for content (Higgsfield, Claude Design Motion)
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model

items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 2, Become an AI Leader
items.quote: Train, don't tell.

items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 2, Become an AI Leader

items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 2, Become an AI Leader

items.item: Teach root principles instead of writing an SOP for every problem
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 2, Become an AI Leader

items.item: New hires spend week one (40 hours) on recorded trainings, then take a test
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 2, Become an AI Leader

items.item: Shout out exceptional people every week

items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 2, Become an AI Leader

items.item: Whole team installs and uses the AI; invite, remind, then decide

items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 1, AI Growth Model

items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula

items.item: Chief of staff chases the team for information in real time to drive AI adoption

items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula

items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula

items.item: Vision big enough for the whole team's goals to fit
items.speaker: Dan Martell
items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 2, Become an AI Leader
items.quote: Your vision has to be big enough for your whole team's dreams and goals to fit

items.item: Write down one decision the team should never have to ask you again

items.talk: Graeme Barlow, Day 1, Fast Team Formula

items.item: Consider a hackathon so everybody builds with AI

items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 2, Become an AI Leader

items.talk: Dan Martell, Day 2, Become an AI Leader
